system: You turn written credit policy into a small policy language, exactly and without adding rules. You reply with only what is asked for.
prompt:
Here is a credit policy as it was written by the product owner:

Applicants must be twenty-one or older and must earn at least eighteen thousand rupees a month; anyone with a default already on file is turned away. Six months of wallet history earns twenty-five points, and so does keeping an average balance of five thousand or more. Twenty-five points is enough to approve. Lend a quarter of monthly income up to twenty thousand rupees, with a two percent fee on the limit.

Write it in the policy language. Reply with only the policy text, no code fence and no commentary. Keep every rule and do not add any. Give each gate a reason that states the actual threshold.

The language, in full:

    policy      "<name>"
    version     <number>
    currency    <CODE>

    decline if  <field> <op> <value> because "<reason>"
    refer   if  <field> <op> <value> because "<reason>"
    score  +<n> if <field> <op> <value> because "<reason>"
    approve if  score >= <n>
    limit       min(<expr>, <expr>)
    fee         <n>% of limit

Operators are < <= > >= == != . Conditions may be joined with 'and' and 'or'. A number is
plain digits. A text value is in double quotes. 'limit' takes an arithmetic expression over
the fields, and min() and max() of two expressions. 'fee' may also be a flat number, and
may be followed by 'per <period>' - though a charge priced per unit of time is rejected by
the compliance lint, so do not use it.

Statement order matters: gates are tested in the order written and the first one that
matches decides, so keep the order of the source document.

The applicant fields available are: age, monthly_income, wallet_months, txn_velocity,
prior_defaults, on_time_repayments, dependants, avg_balance, employment, region,
has_smartphone. 'employment' is one of "salaried", "self-employed", "daily-wage".
'region' must not be used in a decision.

Here is an unrelated policy in the language, as an example of the shape:

policy "Starter"
version 1
currency PKR

decline if age < 18 because "below the legal age to contract"
decline if monthly_income < 25000 because "monthly income below the floor of 25,000"

score +40 if wallet_months >= 12 because "a year of wallet history"
score +30 if on_time_repayments >= 1 because "repaid on time before"

approve if score >= 40
limit min(0.2 * monthly_income, 15000)
fee 3% of limit
response:
policy "CreditPolicy"
version 1
currency INR

decline if age < 21 because "applicant must be twenty-one or older"
decline if monthly_income < 18000 because "applicant must earn at least eighteen thousand rupees a month"
decline if prior_defaults > 0 because "applicant has a default already on file"

score +25 if wallet_months >= 6 because "six months of wallet history earns twenty-five points"
score +25 if avg_balance >= 5000 because "keeping an average balance of five thousand or more earns twenty-five points"

approve if score >= 25
limit min(0.25 * monthly_income, 20000)
fee 2% of limit
